messages:
Jordan: Heads up — starting a dedicated capacity roadmap thread focused on reserved pools, quotas, burst, and autoscaling policy. Need decisions by EOW so we can schedule scope.
Maya: Quick summary of customer asks: 3 customers want burst above baseline for traffic spikes, 1 customer needs hard quota caps for cost governance.
Ravi: Current infra supports reserved pools + a queue-length autoscaler. Limits today: min/max GPUs per pool, no per-customer burst accounting.
Claire: Sales note — HealthCo (healthtech) requires burst for nightly report generation. They'll pay for isolated burst if we can guarantee latency.
Jordan: High-level options: a) soft burst with throttling + usage billing, b) hard reserved burst capacity customers buy, c) queue-based preemption and model fallbacks.
Maya: Engineering constraints: GPU cold-start ~45s. Prefetch helps but 95p latency is hard if we spin GPUs during spikes. Need predictable warm capacity or tokenized bursts.
Ravi: I propose a "burst tokens" model — customers have a burst quota (tokens). When pool saturated, requests can consume tokens to trigger extra capacity or prioritize scheduling.
Claire: Customers like predictable billing. If tokens = dollars, they can reason about cost. Need UI that estimates token burn for common workloads.
Maya: Implementation sketch for autoscaler config:
```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  type: hybrid
  baseline_capacity: 4
  burst_quota: 10000_tokens/month
  burst_rate_limit: 50_tokens/min
  scale_timeout: 60s
```
This keeps autoscale reactive while limiting unbounded spin-ups.
Jordan: Launch criteria (MVP): 1) Console + API to configure burst_quota, 2) Billing meter for token usage, 3) E2E latency SLO test under synthetic spikes, 4) Fallback path to lower-capacity model variant.
Ravi: Operational concerns: accurate accounting, abuse protection (no noisy neighbors), cross-customer fairness. Recommend phased rollout with canary customers and a circuit breaker that stops burst if backend alerts spike.
Maya: Rough effort estimate: runtime + burst hook ~6 weeks, billing and metrics ~2 weeks, console/API ~2 weeks, canary/hardening ~2 weeks => ~10 weeks total for MVP.
Jordan: For prioritization: MVP = token model + console + billing. Defer per-minute dynamic prefetch and per-request model-variant fallback to phase 2.
Claire: Which customers for canary? Recommend HealthCo, QuickDocs, AcmeAds — they already expressed interest and have different traffic patterns.
Maya: @Ravi — does this require infra tagging for burst-eligible nodes or special placement groups?
Ravi: Yes. We'll add node tags and a lightweight accounting agent to track token consumption. Also RBAC for who can allocate burst tokens to accounts. Low infra risk but some bookkeeping.
Jordan: Decision items to close by EOW: (1) accept token model? (2) confirm MVP scope? (3) approve canary customers? Please react with :thumbsup: if you agree.
deploy-bot: Reminder — product review on Thu 11:00. Will sync decision items then.
Claire: :thumbsup: Sales side green.
Maya: :thumbsup: Eng can deliver MVP scope in the estimate above.
Ravi: :thumbsup: SRE ok with infra changes and circuit breaker plan.
Jordan: Great — next steps: Maya drafts spec doc + API schema, Ravi lists infra tasks & monitoring, Claire secures canary agreements. I'll capture OKRs and the scope negotiation notes.
Maya: One more note: quotas should be per-account per-pool. Allowing cross-pool bursting raises complexity for billing and fairness; prefer to keep per-pool scoping for MVP.
